result.title: Debate to Deceive: Poisoning LLM's Fact-Checking via Game-Theoretic Multi-Agent Debate
result.summary: Knowledge attacks on Large Language Models, such as manipulating fact-checking judgments, pose significant risks to AI reliability. Existing approaches -- adversarial suffix/template injection and single-agent self-reflection -- lack robustness across diverse defenses and are prone to confirmation bias and costly trial-and-error, respectively. We propose Debate-to-Deceive (D2D), a multi-agent debate framework grounded in human debate structure and rhetorical style, enabling agents to generate adversarial passages that are semantically coherent, rhetorically effective, and resistant to early confirmation bias. D2D formalizes the adversarial process as an evolutionary game in which agents adaptively evolve their rhetorical strategies (Logos, Pathos, Ethos) through competition. To manage the intractably large LLM output space, we decouple agent behavior into a strategic layer, which selects a rhetorical action from a compact strategy space via evolutionary-inspired learning dynamics, and a generation layer, where the LLM produces a concrete passage conditioned on that strategy and the debate context. On four fact-checking benchmarks (FEVER, HealthVer, CLIMATE-FEVER, and SciFact), D2D substantially outperforms existing attacks and evades most defenses.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Debate-to-Deceive，按人类辩论结构组织多智能体辩论并以演化博弈更新修辞策略，生成语义连贯且抗确认偏误的对抗段落来操纵 LLM 事实核查判断，在四个事实核查基准上优于现有攻击并规避多数防御。
AI.relevance_reason: 其将行为解耦为「紧凑策略层的博弈式选择＋LLM 生成层」，可能为 LVR 中离散潜状态选择、多假设竞争与验证提供结构线索；纯文本对抗设定能否迁移到视觉证据核查需进一步评估。
